items.title: Tule elk rut

location.name: Carrizo Plain, Soda Lake Road foothills

items.reason: Peak of the documented annual cycle, with a recent report near the site.
items.awaiting: Documented annual cycle and a recent report near the site. Conditions and access on the day still matter.

optional: Sony FE 70-200mm f/2.8 GM OSS II for animals in their landscape
skip: Sony FE 2x Teleconverter: dawn light and moving animals need shutter speed more than reach. The 2x costs two stops (f/12.6 on the 200-600), slows autofocus and magnifies shimmer and shake; an APS-C crop of the 61 MP file keeps about 26 MP.
gear.start: 1/1000 s or faster, f/6.3, auto ISO; animal-eye AF, continuous.
gear.support: Beanbag on the car window or a gimbal head; stay in or beside the vehicle
gear.technique: Burst for sparring; backlit breath and dust at first light is the frame.
gear.video: DJI Osmo Pocket 3 for bugling audio
gear.drone: DJI Mini 3: not appropriate - wildlife is the subject, and a drone disturbs it.

items.ethics: Stay in or beside the vehicle; keep well back from bulls.
items.safety_summary: No NWS warnings for this place and time.
safety_notes: Carrizo roads are impassable clay when wet.
items.detail: Bugling, sparring and harem defence, and the whole thing runs on first light. Shoot from the vehicle where possible - it is a far better hide than standing, and keeps you the legal distance back. Backlit dust and breath in dawn light is the shot worth driving for.
